Telescope 4.3 brings thirteen new optional plugins, a Windows 11 camera every app can see and noise reduction for the mic.

## New

**Optional plugins.** All of them start out off. Switch the ones you want on in the Plugins tab of Settings, which is now a grid of tiles sorted into groups and has its own search. Most need no download.

- **Colour grading** with colour wheels, curves, a before and after split and `.cube` LUTs. Each phone gets its own grade and presets save it
- **Chroma key** for a green or blue screen, or one of any colour you click on the preview
- **Cinema tools** adds focus peaking, zebras, false colour, a histogram, waveform, vectorscope and a level from the phone's sensors to the preview
- **Photos** takes real photos with the phone's camera at full quality, from a plain JPEG up to RAW, full sensor resolution, Night mode, bursts and long exposures on phones that can do them
- **Several cameras in one picture** puts your streams side by side, in a grid or in your own layout, for apps that only take one camera
- **Desk mode** straightens anything flat the phone looks at, like a page or a drawing
- **Privacy blur** blurs other people who walk into the picture (or the whole room, or puts the wait screen up)
- **Expose for my face** moves the phone's metering to your face, which helps a lot with a bright window behind you
- **Notes next to the lens** shows your notes in big text right under the front camera so you can read them while still looking almost straight at the people on the call
- **Name tag**, an **On Air sign** for the people you live with and **QR codes**, which copies a code you hold up to the camera (a Wi-Fi code gives you its password)
- **Fun pack** with clones of yourself, an invisibility cloak, light painting, slit-scan, retro looks and datamosh

**Windows 11 camera.** On Windows 11 Telescope now has its own camera that every app can see, including the Windows Camera app and others that never listed the old one. If you already have the old driver installed, **Update** under **Virtual camera & phone** in Settings switches you over. Windows 10 stays on the old driver.

**Mic noise reduction.** A switch on the Microphone card takes typing, fans and room hiss out of the mic on your computer. It works the same for every phone and for Browser camera's mic, which helps most with phones whose own noise suppression is weak.

## Changed

- Dynamic now works with UDP on Wi-Fi. It backs off sooner because the computer reports lost packets to the phone (in my tests a link held to 4 Mbps settled at about 2.5 Mbps with under 1% loss).
- Installing a newer `.zip` of a plugin replaces the old one and keeps its settings. Plugins can link to their repository and Telescope can check it for new releases, or install them automatically if you turn that on.
- **Width** and **Height** on the Transforms card stretch or squish the picture.
- Cards in the main window are sorted by group and share their group's colour with the Plugins tab.

## Fixed

- The Camera card could lose its lens tiles once the lenses loaded.
- Pressing Stop right as a stream moved between USB and Wi-Fi froze the window for about 5 seconds.
- Some translated texts were cut off in switches and in the Settings tab list.

## For plugin makers

- New host services cover what several of the built-in plugins needed: motion zones, steady people tracking, drawing and picking on the preview, frames from other streams, full-quality photos, the phone's sensors, the colour pipeline and the stream's H.264 before it's decoded. `desktop/ARCHITECTURE.md` describes them.
- `plugin.json` takes a `category` (the Plugins tab group) and a `repo` link.
